title: Get started with tvcQGComp
text: tvcQGComp estimates survival effect joint interventions quantized time-varying exposure mixture. core workflow : arrange observed data long person-period format; define outcome, exposures, covariates, histories, estimand; validate data configuration; generate quantized intervention scenarios; run Monte Carlo g-computation; use subject-level bootstrap confidence intervals. public release focuses main-effect survival analyses quantized exposures.

title: Get started with tvcQGComp
text: input must contain one row per subject follow-interval. minimum, configured columns must identify: Subject identifiers interval times uniquely identify rows. Base variables used model formulas must present, correctly typed, supported every time required simulation. Lagged formula terms need stored input auto_history = TRUE.

title: Get started with tvcQGComp
text: package includes complete simulated dataset used example. configuration analysis contract. finalized fitting point estimate bootstrap stages use identical models interventions. simple example, age income_inadequacy used baseline/time-fixed adjustment variables, seven neighborhood urban-form covariates simulated forward active time-varying covariates.
code: library(tvcQGComp)  data("sim_data", package = "tvcQGComp") dat <- sim_data dat$TimeOut <- as.integer(as.character(dat$TimeOut))  exposures <- c("BC", "NIT", "SO4", "NH4", "OM") active_tvc <- c(   "Urban_form", "CanadianRegion", "CSize", "deprivation",   "dependency", "instability", "ethnicconcentration" ) baseline <- c(   "age", "income_inadequacy", "sex", "visible_minority",   "IndigenousIdentity", "marsth", "Education", "employment", "Occupation" )  # These are formula term names only. auto_history creates the columns. active_lag_terms <- paste0(active_tvc, "_lag1") tvc_formulas <- setNames(lapply(active_tvc, function(response) {   reformulate(     c(       "TimeOut", "I(TimeOut^2)", baseline,       setdiff(active_lag_terms, paste0(response, "_lag1"))     ),     response = response   ) }), active_tvc)  cfg <- make_tvcqgcomp_config(   id = "UniqID",   time_in = "TimeInn",   time_out = "TimeOut",   outcome = "status",   exposures = exposures,   time_varying_covariates = active_tvc,   time_fixed_covariates = baseline,   factor_vars = c("income_inadequacy", active_tvc, baseline),   outcome_formula = reformulate(     c(exposures, "TimeOut", "I(TimeOut^2)", baseline, active_tvc),     response = "status"   ),   tvc_formulas = tvc_formulas,   covtypes = c(     setNames(rep("categorical", length(active_tvc)), active_tvc)   ),   q = 4,   exposome = "quantized",   natural_course = "calibration",   auto_history = TRUE,   baselags = TRUE,   meta_target = c("HR", "RR", "RD") )  validate_tvcqgcomp_data(dat, cfg)

title: Time-Varying Quantile G-Computation (tvcQGcomp)
text: complete, explicitly specified implementation installed system.file("examples", "simulated-survival-analysis.R", package = "tvcQGComp"). includes outcome model, time-varying covariate models, HR/RR/RD meta-models, parallel bootstrap settings, code combines non-bootstrap point estimates bootstrap percentile confidence intervals. bundled dataset contains 5,584 person-period records 500 simulated individuals followed 1 13 years. Exactly 100 participants die follow-, giving 20% cumulative mortality. five exposures continuous quantized internally package. Lagged variables deliberately absent auto_history = TRUE creates preparation. contains real participant data. data also available RDS file system.file("extdata", "sim_data_500.RDS", package = "tvcQGComp").
code: library(tvcQGComp)  data("sim_data", package = "tvcQGComp") dat <- sim_data dat$TimeOut <- as.integer(as.character(dat$TimeOut))  exposures <- c("BC", "NIT", "SO4", "NH4", "OM") active_tvc <- c(   "Urban_form", "CanadianRegion", "CSize", "deprivation",   "dependency", "instability", "ethnicconcentration" ) baseline <- c(   "age", "income_inadequacy", "sex", "visible_minority",   "IndigenousIdentity", "marsth", "Education", "employment", "Occupation" )  # These are formula term names only. auto_history creates the columns. active_lag_terms <- paste0(active_tvc, "_lag1") tvc_formulas <- setNames(lapply(active_tvc, function(response) {   reformulate(     c(       "TimeOut", "I(TimeOut^2)", baseline,       setdiff(active_lag_terms, paste0(response, "_lag1"))     ),     response = response   ) }), active_tvc)  cfg <- make_tvcqgcomp_config(   id = "UniqID",   time_in = "TimeInn",   time_out = "TimeOut",   outcome = "status",   exposures = exposures,   time_varying_covariates = active_tvc,   time_fixed_covariates = baseline,   factor_vars = c(     "income_inadequacy", active_tvc, baseline   ),   outcome_formula = reformulate(     c(exposures, "TimeOut", "I(TimeOut^2)", baseline, active_tvc),     response = "status"   ),   tvc_formulas = tvc_formulas,   covtypes = c(     setNames(rep("categorical", length(active_tvc)), active_tvc)   ),   q = 4,   exposome = "quantized",   natural_course = "calibration",   auto_history = TRUE,   baselags = TRUE,   meta_target = c("HR", "RR", "RD") )  scenarios <- generate_intervention_scenarios(cfg)  fit <- tvcQGComp_survival(   data = dat,   config = cfg,   mc_size = 1000,   intervention_scenarios = scenarios,   seed = 1234 )  # Default printing focuses on model-based effects. print(fit)  # Request time-specific risk and survival predictions only when needed. print(fit, prediction = "trajectory")  # The primary plot is cumulative incidence by quantile. plot_cumulative_risk_trajectory(   fit,   include_natural = FALSE,   include_average = TRUE )  # Draw survival curves only when they are needed. plot_survival_trajectory(   fit,   include_natural = FALSE,   include_average = TRUE )  # Use larger values for final analyses. boot <- tvcQGComp_survival_boot(   data = dat,   config = cfg,   n_boot = 200,   mc_size = 10000,   intervention_scenarios = scenarios,   seed = 1234,   parallel = TRUE,   n_workers = 4,   batch_size = 4 )  summarize_tvcqgcomp_bootstrap(boot)

title: Create a tvcQGcomp Configuration and Quantized Scenarios — make_tvcqgcomp_config
text: id Subject identifier column name. time_in Start--interval time column name. time_name Alternative name time_in. time_out End--interval time column name. outcome Outcome column name. outcome_type Outcome type. current public release supports "survival" pooled person-time survival analyses. exposures Exposure column names. exposure_lags Lagged exposure column names. Defaults paste0(exposures, "_lag1"). exposure_formulas Optional formulas modeled natural-course exposures. exposure_types Named vector exposure model types. Supported values include "categorical", "multinomial", "binary", "normal", "bounded_normal", "bounded_normal_snap", ordinal-logit aliases "ordinal", "ordinal_logit", "ordinal_polr", "ordered_logit", "polr". time_varying_covariates Time-varying confounder column names. tvc_lags Lagged time-varying confounder column names. covtypes Named vector time-varying confounder model types. Supported values include "categorical", "multinomial", "binary", "normal", "bounded_normal", "bounded_normal_snap", ordinal-logit aliases "ordinal", "ordinal_logit", "ordinal_polr", "ordered_logit", "polr". passive_tvc_vars Optional subset time_varying_covariates carry forward sampled observed id-time path without fitting stochastic TVC model. Passive TVCs remain available outcome, exposure, confounder formulas time point. time_fixed_covariates Baseline covariates stay fixed within subject. factor_vars Variables treated factors simulation prediction. outcome_formula Outcome model formula. tvc_formulas Named list time-varying confounder model formulas. q Primary quantization level argument. NULL, function falls back q_levels (4). q_levels Number quantile levels used define intervention grid. natural_course One natural-course modes. preferred names "none", "calibration", "observed_exposome", "modeled_exposome". Backward-compatible aliases "observed" "modeled" also accepted normalized "calibration" "modeled_exposome", respectively. "calibration" predicts outcomes observed data path without forward simulation; "observed_exposome" forward-simulates TVCs keeping sampled observed exposure histories fixed; "modeled_exposome" forward-simulates TVCs exposures. auto_history Logical; whether generate required lag histories base variables data preparation. TRUE, lag columns referenced configuration model formulas need present input data. baselags Logical scalar following gfoRmula convention early lag histories pre-baseline rows unavailable. FALSE, early *_lag2, *_lag3, etc. values set 0 numeric variables reference level factors. TRUE, early lag values set subject's baseline value. meta_target Second-stage summary target. Use "HR" pooled hazard-based person-time multiplicative meta model, "HD" pooled hazard-based additive meta model, "RR" end--follow-cumulative-risk ratio meta model, "RD" end--follow-cumulative-risk difference meta model. Multiple targets can requested, example c("HR", "HD") c("RR", "RD"); legacy shortcut "" expands c("HR", "RR"). Historical aliases "hazard" "cumrisk_final" also accepted. categorical_sim Categorical simulation rule time-varying covariates modeled exposures. "stochastic" uses multinomial probability draws; "class" uses deterministic class prediction. exposome Exposure representation. Use "quantized" current public release. exposure_scale Backward-compatible alias exposome. bounded_supports Optional named list specifying legal support grids bounded-normal snap/ordinal variables. entry can numeric vector (example 1:5), list(values = ...), list(min=, max=, =), "observed" use observed unique values. data Observed data validate. config tvcQGcomp configuration object. levels Intervention levels assign exposures. Defaults 0:(q_levels - 1). prefix Scenario name prefix.

title: Run the tvcQGcomp Pipeline — run_tvcqgcomp
text: data Observed input data. config tvcQGcomp configuration object. mc_size Monte Carlo sample size. intervention_scenarios Named list static quantized intervention values. natural_course subset preferred labels "calibration", "observed_exposome", "modeled_exposome", "none". Backward-compatible aliases "observed" "modeled" also accepted. "calibration" predicts outcomes observed data path, "observed_exposome" forward-simulates TVCs keeping sampled observed exposure histories, "modeled_exposome" forward-simulates TVCs exposures. seed Random seed Monte Carlo resampling simulation. replace_mc Whether sample subjects replacement creating Monte Carlo skeleton. meta_formula Optional pooled meta-model formula. meta_family Optional model family pooled meta model. single target requested meta_family NULL, defaults quasibinomial("logit") "HR", gaussian("identity") "HD", quasibinomial("identity") "RD", quasibinomial("log") "RR". multiple meta targets requested, pass either NULL use defaults target named list list(HR = quasibinomial("logit"), HD = gaussian("identity")). meta_target Second-stage summary target. Use "HR", "HD", "RR", "RD", vector c("HR", "HD"). Historical aliases "hazard" "cumrisk_final" also accepted; legacy shortcut "" expands c("HR", "RR"). multiple targets requested, first-stage simulation run requested second-stage meta-models fit simulated intervention data. fit_meta Optional logical controlling whether second-stage meta-model fit. Defaults TRUE quantized exposures. FALSE, risk_trajectory still reports time-specific scenario risks survival, HR, HD, RR, RD effect estimate produced. fit_exposure_models Optional logical controlling whether exposure evolution models fit. Defaults FALSE natural_course = "none" every intervention scenario deterministically assigns every exposure; otherwise defaults TRUE. exposure_scale Exposure representation used first-stage fitting simulation. minimal release, use "quantized". quantization_breaks Optional fixed cutpoints used exposure_scale = "quantized". joint_effect_fn Optional function mapping scenario vector scalar joint effect. verbose Logical; print progress status messages fitting simulation.

title: tvcQGComp 0.0.0
text: Initial public GitHub release. Supports quantized static intervention scenarios time-varying exposure mixtures. Provides model-based HR, RR, RD main-effect estimates pooled person-time final-risk meta models. Includes cluster bootstrap support confidence intervals. Includes simulated longitudinal survival dataset reproducible example analysis. Includes cumulative-incidence survival trajectory plots, including optional average line across quantized scenarios. Includes run drift diagnostics model checking.
